title: Recoverability as a System Primitive for Long-Horizon AI Agents
abstract: arXiv:2609.13672v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI agents can be interrupted while editing files, calling tools, or carrying out multi-step tasks. Restarting repeats completed work, but continuing from unverified or outdated progress can carry earlier errors forward. A saved state is not necessarily a suitable place to resume. We introduce recoverability as a system primitive that makes reuse an explicit decision: select a supported starting point and a permitted recovery action, or withhold automatic continuation. Its behavioral contract binds that choice to supporting evidence, execution, and independent checks. A reference architecture connects persistence, validation, and control, with complementary runtime instances testing distinct responsibilities. Four deterministic and 20 paired file challenges demonstrate that accurate restoration and successful completion can conceal disallowed starting points. Progress controls attribute retained work to shared restoration. Event-time test

translated_title: 可恢复性作为长时程AI智能体的系统原语
translated_abstract: AI智能体在编辑文件、调用工具或执行多步任务时可能会被中断。重新启动会重复已完成的工作，但从未经证实或过时的进度继续则可能将早期的错误延续下去。保存的状态并不一定就是合适的恢复起点。我们提出将“可恢复性”作为一种系统原语，使复用成为一个明确的决策：选择一个受支持的起始点和被允许的恢复操作，或者暂停自动继续。其行为契约将这一选择与支持证据、执行和独立检查绑定在一起。一个参考架构连接了持久化、验证和控制，互补的运行时实例分别测试不同的职责。四个确定性和20个成对文件挑战表明，准确的恢复和成功的完成可能会掩盖不被允许的起始点。进度控制将保留的工作归因于共享的恢复机制。
tldr: 本文提出将“可恢复性”作为长时程AI智能体的系统原语，使从保存状态恢复成为一个基于证据验证的明确决策，避免盲目继续可能携带先前错误的进度。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces recoverability as a system primitive for long-horizon AI agents, making resume-from-saved-state an explicit, evidence-verified decision rather than blindly continuing with progress that may carry forward earlier errors.
